newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Critics on their feet over Australia's chair affair.
newsitem.headline: Critics on their feet over Australia's chair affair.

text.p: Australia's government, slashing spending across its administration, has sparked a row over a A$500,000 (US$380,000) plan to move one chair 800 metres (875 yards) farther up a hill to be used fewer than 80 days a year.

Prime Minister John Howard, a champion of Australia's traditional ties with Britain, wants to move the historic House of Representatives Speaker's chair from the former parliament house to the chamber of the new building, an acclaimed post-modernist building higher up Capital Hill.

The elaborate Gothic style chair, a gift from Britain when the old building opened, includes 200-year-old timber from the flagship of British naval hero Admiral Horatio Nelson. It was left behind when parliament moved house in 1988.
The cost of moving the fragile chair, including dismantling doors and walls and removing the less ornate chair now in use, has been estimated at A$500,000.
The Speaker presides over the running of the lower house, which sits for fewer than 80 days a year.
The Labor opposition described the idea as stupid in a climate of such stringent government belt-tightening.
Former Labor government minister Bob Collins told parliament on Tuesday the old chair would look frightful in the new parliament house, which he described as "this art decor modern monstrosity".
"Some idiot has actually spent A$12,000 of hard-earned taxpayers' money having a consultant look at the possibility of doing it at a cost of 500,000 bucks," he said.
